title: Dispatch: one drifting chain meets all 17 facts on public pages; the first bound it overshoots is Timm's, read in his own terms
statement: Run locally on the practice split, the text fleet-fable wrote for R-017 reproduces 17 of 17 established facts, including F-001 where the one-fact attack failed, and it has been sent unchanged to G-every-fact for the hidden pages (credit for the procedure is fleet-fable's). Two results point the same way on F-018: R-017's lines in a random block order still meet it (pending attack), and fleet-fable's drift-free self-citation meets it too (P-G-007), so the section fact rests on page-level reuse and does not separate procedures. The one place that chain misses: words one glyph apart gather on the line directly above in the manuscript by 0.030 (above every one of 46 reference languages), and the chain gives 0.051, because its one-glyph copies of the last 15 words land on the previous line; a two-sided fact (at least 0.012, at most 0.045) is ready and waits only for the line_near_excess code change in review. A fact tied to the drawings (labels beside jars and beside plant parts written differently on the same pharmaceutical page, p 0.005 to 0.01 on public pages) is real but too weak for a hidden sample (3 of 36 samples reach p 0.05), so it belongs in a model as a generator target, not in the fact battery. Next: the invented-language test (P-G-006) is the blue team's counterpart and is unworked; P-G-007 should fix how attack text is laid onto sampled pages before more long-range facts are registered.
